item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 251754
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several hundred miles
west of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on
Tropical Storm Julio, located well west-southwest of the southern
tip of Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the
trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical
depression is likely to form during the latter part of the week or
early this weekend while the system drifts northeastward, then
turns to the west-northwest.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week. Some gradual development is possible by
the weekend into early next week while the system moves slowly to
the west or west-northwest, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Blake
NNNN

item.description:

000

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  54
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...LALA EXPECTED TO BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE IN A COUPLE OF 
DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...35.0N 177.2W
ABOUT 525 MI...845 KM N OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 460 MI...740 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 35.0 North, longitude 177.2 West.  Lala is
moving toward the west-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h) and a slow 
west-northwestward to northwestward motion is expected over the 
next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual weakening is expected during the next 48 hours, and Lala 
is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low on Thursday.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 54
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 252032
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  54
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Tue Aug 25 2026

Deep convection associated with Lala has decreased a bit in 
coverage over the past few hours.  Whereas this may be temporary, 
it is more likely a response to cooler waters.  The system 
continues to exhibit a ragged eye-like feature and remains fairly 
well organized.  The intensity is held at 45 kt for this advisory 
which is the same as a Dvorak Current Intensity Number from the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center.  Dvorak Final T-Numbers have 
decreased however.  Data from an upcoming scatterometer overpass 
should provide a good intensity estimate.

Lala continues moving west-northwestward, with an initial motion 
estimate of 300/5 kt.  A mid-level ridge to the northeast of the 
cyclone should steer the system on a west-northwestward to 
northwestward track for the next few days.  Since Lala is likely to 
remain fairly well removed from the faster southwesterly flow at 
higher latitudes for the next 72 hours, it is likely to continue 
moving rather slowly until late in the forecast period.  Not much 
change is made to the official track forecast for this advisory 
cycle.  The official forecast remains close to the corrected model 
consensus, HCCA, solution.

The cyclone is likely to remain over relatively cooler waters of 
around 23 deg C or so and within a fairly dry low- to mid-level air 
mass during the forecast period.  Therefore, gradual weakening is 
expected and Lala will probably degenerate into a post-tropical 
cyclone within 60 hours, or sooner.  This is consistent with the 
latest simulated IR imagery from the ECMWF which shows most of the 
system's deep convection dissipating by that time.
